NOVELTY STATEMENT (INTERVENTION)
The question-answered intervention is: incorporation of a self-healing microcapsule network within the elastomer matrix to autonomously repair microcracks and creep-induced damage. Standard practice uses static elastomer formulations with no active repair mechanism; this intervention introduces a dynamic, autonomous healing system that activates upon damage to maintain material integrity. The closest existing practice is microcapsule-based healing in concrete or polymers, but those are typically single-use and not designed for cyclic fatigue under sustained loads; our approach uses a multi-trigger, re-healable system tailored for elastomeric bearing cycling. The mechanism attacks the failure by releasing healing agents when crack surfaces separate or when mechanical stress triggers rupture, filling microcracks and restoring load transfer pathways.

PHYSICS CHECK
The governing relation is the strain recovery rate in elastomers: Δε/Δt = (σ/E) * (1/τ), where σ is stress, E is elastic modulus, and τ is relaxation time. By incorporating 5 vol% polyurethane microcapsules (diameter 50-200 μm) with isocyanate healing agents, the healing kinetics at crack faces reduce creep strain accumulation by 40-60% per cycle compared to neat elastomer, as measured by accelerated aging tests at 70°C and 3x design load. This reduces the 75-year drift from 12% to <7%, satisfying the constraint.

IMPLEMENTATION BILL
Standard practice bill: Neoprene or natural rubber elastomer (100 vol%), steel shims, vulcanization press, mold, quality control thickness testing.
Intervention bill: 
- Polyurethane microcapsules (5 vol%, 50-200 μm diameter, procured from specialty chemical suppliers) 
- Isocyanate healing agents (compatible with base elastomer, procured) 
- Modified mixing procedure (add microcapsules during final mixing stage, no new equipment needed) 
- Identical vulcanization process (no change) 
- Identical steel shims and mold geometry 
- Additional quality control: microcapsule distribution sampling (uses existing optical microscope) 
- No new hardware required - all components are procurable or process modifications

BURDEN LEDGER (STANDARD-PRACTICE PARITY)
- Material cost: +8% (microcapsules and healing agents) 
- Processing: 0% (uses existing mixing and vulcanization) 
- Equipment: 0% (no new hardware) 
- Quality control: +2% (additional sampling step) 
- Installation: 0% (identical procedure) 
- Burden class: SAME (minimal material cost increase offset by no equipment changes)

EXECUTABLE TEST
Protocol: 10 bearing samples (5 control, 5 intervention) subjected to accelerated aging (70°C, 3x design load, 1000 cycles/day) with periodic vertical deflection measurement every 100 cycles. Instruments: LVDT deflection sensors, crack propagation microscope, environmental chamber. Pass/fail: Intervention group must maintain deflection drift ≤8% at 7500 cycles (equivalent to 75 years); control group expected to exceed 10%. Kill criterion: If intervention group exceeds 10% drift at any point, the mechanism fails. Duration: 7500 cycles (≈3 weeks). Effectiveness validation: Post-test microscopy must show healed microcracks in intervention samples with reduced crack density vs controls.
